title: Nếp cái hoa vàng lên truyền hình phường
excerpt: Truyền hình Nhị Chiểu làm phóng sự về nếp cái hoa vàng của phường.

cover.alt: Máy gặt trên cánh đồng nếp cái hoa vàng ở phường Nhị Chiểu

bodyHtml:
UBND phường Nhị Chiểu, TP. Hải Phòng, đăng phóng sự “Nếp cái hoa vàng phường Nhị Chiểu – lan tỏa hương vị đặc sản quê hương” của Truyền hình Nhị Chiểu.

Phóng sự quay cánh đồng nếp cái hoa vàng vào mùa gặt, khi máy gặt đang vào ruộng.

title: From a farm supply shop to a bag of rice with our village's name
excerpt: Thirteen years of selling seed to local farmers, then one day the family took its own village rice to market.

cover.alt: A stack of Duy Tân sticky rice bags with the printed logo

bodyHtml:
Since 2008, the family has run a shop that sells farm supplies and yellow-flower sticky rice seed to farmers in the area.

In 2021, with encouragement from the local farming cooperative, the family decided to bring the village's yellow-flower sticky rice to market itself. The seed is chosen with care, and family members tend each field themselves. The cooperative helped buy a small vacuum sealer that packs one 2 kg bag at a time, and designed the first bag. That year, 10 tonnes of rice, about 5,000 bags, reached customers.

One step each year

In 2022, the family added a dryer and a rice mill, and output grew to 30 tonnes. In 2023–2024, the rice was packed in neat square packs, each labelled by hand, and reached supermarket shelves. In 2024, the product received a 3-star OCOP rating and a new food safety certificate. In 2025, the logo was printed directly on the bag, and the family produced 50 tonnes of rice.

See all the milestones in the Journey section on the home page.

title: One drying batch of 20 tonnes
excerpt: Why the sticky rice paddy is dried right at home, and how one drying batch works.

cover.alt: The family's rice mill and paddy dryer

bodyHtml:
In 2022, as orders grew, the family invested in a paddy dryer that takes 20 tonnes per batch.

Hot air rises from below

A fan blows hot air from a coal furnace into the space under the dryer. The hot air rises through a steel mesh and dries the layer of paddy on top.

Dry first, then mill

The dry paddy goes into the rice mill: the husks blow out, and the white grains flow down. Then the rice is vacuum-sealed in 2 kg bags.

title: Steaming soft, fragrant yellow-flower sticky rice
excerpt: A few simple steps for a pot of steamed sticky rice that is soft, fragrant and evenly cooked.
bodyHtml:
Rinse the sticky rice gently, then soak it in clean water for 6–8 hours, or overnight. Lift it out, mix in a little salt, and let it drain.

Steaming

Put the rice in a steamer once the water boils, and steam it for about 25–30 minutes. Halfway through, open the lid, stir it well and pour a few spoons of hot water over it, so the grains cook evenly.

The rice is done when the grains are clear and soft, with no hard centre. For shiny, fragrant rice, mix in a spoon of scallion oil or coconut milk as soon as the rice is cooked.

title: Storing vacuum-packed sticky rice
excerpt: How long a 2 kg bag of sticky rice keeps, and how to store it once it is open.

cover.alt: Rows of square 2 kg sticky rice packs

bodyHtml:
Each 2 kg bag of sticky rice is vacuum-sealed right after milling, so the rice stays dry and keeps its fragrance.

While the bag is still sealed

Keep it in a dry, cool, airy place, out of the sun. The use-by date on the bag is 12 months from the date of production.

Once the bag is open

Pour the rice into a jar with a tight lid, and keep it in a dry, cool place away from the stove. Use it within about 1–2 months, while the rice is still fragrant.
